correctness.rationale: In characteristic zero at most five distinct binary fourth-power directions are independent, so any line has exactly two nonzero direction classes of sizes 2 and 2 or 2 and 3. A component pair is a full size-two class, with unique phase. Disjoint pairs give 5 × 3 × 4² = 240 intersections; the adjacency of the coordinate-pair types is connected. At a crossing the invertible four-equation Jacobian eliminates the four chart variables, and both off-diagonal solutions vanish on both axes. The residual coefficient is divisible by e²f² and its order-four quotient is 6. Away from a crossing the triple has nonzero coordinates 1,p,q; the repaired chart explicitly has rank four. The residual coefficient is divisible by E² with constant quotient 6(q⁶/p⁴+q²) = -6q²/p⁴, using 1+p⁴+q⁴=0, so there is no higher thickening or extra transverse direction. Completed Fitting ideals are generated by the formal gradient: at the crossings this is (u²v,uv²) with length-one quotient of (uv), and elsewhere it cuts out the reduced branch. The normalization sequence gives 1 - (40(1-3) - 240) = 321 for the reduced arithmetic genus.
residual_risks: The review uses exact formal algebra over C, not a machine proof. The supplied script checks incidence and crossing jets only; it does not certify the noncrossing completed ring or all orders of the elimination.

value.rationale: The complete local-ring classification resolves the punctual structure at common lines of this natural Fano scheme. It distinguishes the nonreduced scheme itself, which has no embedded points, from its intrinsic singular subscheme, which has an embedded length-one contribution at all 240 crossings. This difference is invisible in a list of components or generic multiplicities and is useful for computations on the singular scheme.
residual_risks: The result is specific to this smooth complex diagonal quartic; neither a deformation claim nor a conic-scheme claim follows.
